newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices flat to up 1/8 pt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices flat to up 1/8 pt.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond cash prices ended unchanged to 1/8 point higher Friday, shored up by stronger gains in U.S. Treasuries.
"It was more of a government market rally today than munis," a trader said. "I think prices were up begrudgingly in spots by maybe 1/8 of a point, not any real volume."

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 14/32 at 98-14/32 to yield 6.75 percent. The higher close marked the end of a week-long slump, and stemmed from the Federal Reserve's purchase of coupons as well as shortcovering.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract closed up 7/32 at 116-26/32. The September T-bond contract closed up 15/32 at 111-20/32. The MOB spread was 166 ticks.
Back in munis, players were mindful of the short July 4 holiday work week, which is expected to bring only scant supply, the trader said.
Negotiated and competitive deals are expected to total just $1.16 billion next week, far short of this week's roughly $7 billion in sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

"I don't know if that's necessarily going to be good for prices unless we start seeing some wirehouse business," the trader said, referring to firms that have access to a large number of retail investors.

"Yields probably went up 10 to 15 basis points this week, probably closer to 10 in most cases, and if that attracts any wirehouse business then you could start getting some bonds taken out of the market," he said.
On the other hand, the market may just mark time next week to see how the overall interest rate picture develops, and what happens with supply heading into July, the trader said.
"People could just basically fake it I think," he said.
The Federal Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday and Wednesday, but no rate action is expected.
